sentience.description:
Welcome to Sentience Robotics
Welcome to the official documentation for Sentience Robotics, an open-source initiative dedicated to developing a modular, full-stack framework for humanoid interaction and control.
Our mission is to bridge the gap between high-level AI-driven cognition and robust, real-time hardware execution. While our primary development thrives on the InMoov platform (created by Gael Langevin), our architecture is built to be a universal "brain and nervous system" adaptable to any humanoid hardware.

Our Core Projects
The Sentience ecosystem is powered by two specialized pillars:
• LUCY | The Platform Bridge: Our ROS 2-based interface layer. Lucy abstracts hardware complexity, using a C++ core and ros2_control to allow external web clients or AI models to command robotic actuators seamlessly.
• HuRI | Human-Robot Interaction: The AI framework focusing on Speech-to-Speech (S2S) pipelines, multi-layer cognitive memory (short, medium, and long-term), and kinematic grounding to ensure robot movements feel natural and context-aware.

Our Open Source Pledge
We believe the future of robotics should not be locked behind proprietary doors. Sentience Robotics is committed to the Open Source movement.
• Accessibility: We provide our tools, research, and documentation freely to lower the barrier to entry for researchers and makers.
• Licensing: Our software is primarily licensed under GPL-3.0, while our hardware contributions respect the CC BY-NC roots of the InMoov project.

💡 Join the Evolution
We aren't just building a robot; we are building a community. We are incredibly eager to hear your thoughts, critique our methods, and see how you implement our stack.
• Contribute: Whether you are a ROS 2 expert, an AI researcher, or a 3D printing enthusiast, your contributions are welcome.
• Feedback: Your insights help us iterate faster. We value every bug report, feature suggestion, and architectural discussion.
• Connect: Join our Discord Community (discord.gg/g4KNZ3eeBd) to exchange ideas, share your own projects, or get involved with our teams.

Let’s build the future of humanoid interaction together.
